faq.q: What's the difference between torque and horsepower?
faq.a: Torque is rotational force measured in lb-ft or Nm, while horsepower is the rate of doing work. The formula is: Horsepower = (Torque × RPM) ÷ 5,252. Torque determines acceleration feel and pulling power, while horsepower determines top speed capability.

faq.q: Which is more important for performance - torque or horsepower?
faq.a: Both torque and horsepower matter for different aspects of vehicle behavior. High torque provides strong acceleration and pulling power, especially at lower RPMs. High horsepower supports higher-speed operation. The shape of the torque curve also affects drivability.

faq.q: Why do torque and horsepower curves cross at 5,252 RPM?
faq.a: Torque and horsepower curves mathematically cross at 5,252 RPM due to the conversion formula constants. Below this RPM, torque numbers appear higher than horsepower; above 5,252 RPM, horsepower numbers are higher. This crossover point is purely mathematical.

faq.q: How do I interpret dynamometer (dyno) results?
faq.a: When analyzing dyno results, look at both peak numbers and curve shapes. Broad, flat torque curves provide better drivability than narrow, peaky curves. Consider the RPM range where you'll actually drive the vehicle, not just peak power numbers.

faq.q: How do I convert between different torque and power units?
faq.a: Our calculator handles conversions between lb-ft and Nm for torque, and HP and kW for power. 1 lb-ft = 1.356 Nm, and 1 HP = 0.746 kW. The calculator automatically converts between these units for accurate comparisons.

faq.q: What makes a good torque curve for street driving?
faq.a: For street driving, many people prefer a broad, flat torque curve. This provides more consistent power delivery across a wide RPM range and can make the engine easier to drive in typical conditions. Peak torque at lower RPMs can also improve response at everyday speeds.
